Table program.risk_register {
  risk_register_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique identifier for the risk register entry. Primary key for the risk register product.']
  approved_by_staff_member_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to workforce.staff_member. Business justification: Risk register approval authority must be linked to staff for governance, escalation workflows, and donor risk management reporting requirements.']
  compliance_incident_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to compliance.incident. Business justification: When program risks materialize, they become compliance incidents requiring investigation and corrective action. Essential for linking risk management to incident response in nonprofit operations.']
  intervention_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the program intervention to which this risk applies. Links risk to the specific humanitarian or development program.']
  affected_sdg varchar [note: 'Reference to the Sustainable Development Goal(s) that may be impacted if this risk materializes. Supports alignment with global development frameworks and donor reporting.']
  affected_sector varchar [note: 'Program sector(s) that would be impacted by the risk (e.g., WASH, Health, Nutrition, Education, Protection, Livelihoods). Supports sector-specific risk analysis and reporting.']
  approval_date date [note: 'Date when the risk assessment and mitigation plan were formally approved. Supports governance and audit trail requirements.']
  closure_date date [note: 'Date when the risk was formally closed, either because it was fully mitigated, no longer relevant, or the program ended. Supports risk lifecycle completion tracking.']
  contingency_plan varchar [note: 'Detailed response plan to be activated if the risk materializes. Includes trigger points, escalation procedures, alternative delivery mechanisms, and resource reallocation strategies.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this risk register record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail and data lineage.']
  donor_visibility_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this risk must be reported to donors as part of grant compliance requirements. True if donor reporting is required; false otherwise.']
  effective_end_date date [note: 'Date until which this version of the risk assessment is effective. Null for the current active version. Supports temporal tracking and historical risk analysis.']
  effective_start_date date [note: 'Date from which this version of the risk assessment is effective. Supports temporal tracking and historical risk analysis.']
  escalation_required_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the risk requires escalation to senior management or board level due to its severity or potential organizational impact. True if escalation is required; false otherwise.']
  geographic_scope varchar [note: 'Geographic area(s) affected by the risk (country, region, district, project site). Supports location-based risk mapping and field operations planning.']
  identification_date date [note: 'Date when the risk was first identified and entered into the risk register. Supports risk lifecycle tracking and audit trails.']
  impact_rating varchar [note: 'Qualitative assessment of the severity of consequences if the risk materializes. Considers impact on beneficiaries, program objectives, organizational reputation, and donor relations.']
  impact_score varchar [note: 'Numeric score representing the severity of impact if the risk occurs, typically on a scale of 1-5 where 1 is very low and 5 is very high. Used for quantitative risk prioritization.']
  inherent_risk_score varchar [note: 'Calculated risk score before mitigation measures are applied, typically the product of likelihood_score and impact_score. Represents the raw exposure level.']
  last_modified_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this risk register record was most recently updated. Supports audit trail and change tracking.']
  last_review_date date [note: 'Date when the risk was most recently reviewed and assessed. Supports compliance with donor requirements for periodic risk review (typically quarterly or semi-annually).']
  likelihood_rating varchar [note: 'Qualitative assessment of the probability that the risk will materialize during the program lifecycle. Typically rated on a five-point scale aligned with organizational risk appetite.']
  likelihood_score varchar [note: 'Numeric score representing the likelihood of risk occurrence, typically on a scale of 1-5 where 1 is very low and 5 is very high. Used for quantitative risk prioritization.']
  mitigation_strategy varchar [note: 'Detailed description of the measures, controls, and actions planned or implemented to reduce the likelihood or impact of the risk. Includes preventive and detective controls.']
  next_review_date date [note: 'Scheduled date for the next formal review of the risk. Ensures timely reassessment and supports proactive risk management.']
  notes varchar [note: 'Additional free-text notes, observations, or context related to the risk. Captures supplementary information not covered in structured fields.']
  residual_risk_score varchar [note: 'Calculated risk score after mitigation measures are applied. Represents the remaining exposure after controls are in place. Used to assess whether risk is within acceptable tolerance.']
  revision_reason varchar [note: 'Explanation for why the risk assessment was updated or revised. Captures the business rationale for changes in likelihood, impact, or mitigation strategy.']
  risk_category varchar [note: 'Classification of the risk type. Operational risks relate to program delivery; contextual risks relate to external environment (security, political); institutional risks relate to organizational capacity; fiduciary risks relate to financial management and compliance; programmatic risks relate to program design and effectiveness; reputational risks relate to organizational standing.']
  risk_code varchar [note: 'Unique business identifier for the risk entry, typically following organizational risk coding standards (e.g., OPR-001, CTX-045). Used for cross-referencing in donor reports and internal risk management systems.']
  risk_description varchar [note: 'Detailed narrative description of the risk, including the nature of the threat, potential triggers, and context. Captures the full scope of the risk scenario.']
  risk_level varchar [note: 'Overall risk classification based on the combination of likelihood and impact, determining the priority and urgency of response. Critical risks require immediate escalation and board-level attention.']
  risk_owner varchar [note: 'Name or role of the individual accountable for monitoring the risk and ensuring mitigation measures are implemented. Typically a senior program or operations manager.']
  risk_owner_email varchar [note: 'Email address of the risk owner for communication and escalation purposes.']
  risk_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the risk. Open indicates newly identified; monitoring indicates active tracking; mitigated indicates controls are effective; closed indicates risk no longer relevant; materialized indicates risk has occurred.']
  risk_subcategory varchar [note: 'More granular classification within the risk category (e.g., security incident, supply chain disruption, fraud, partner capacity, beneficiary access). Allows for detailed risk taxonomy alignment.']
  risk_title varchar [note: 'Short, descriptive title of the risk for quick identification and reporting purposes.']
  version_number varchar [note: 'Sequential version number of the risk register entry. Incremented each time the risk assessment is updated, supporting risk evolution tracking across the program lifecycle.']

  Note: 'Risk register entry for a program intervention, capturing risk description, category (operational, contextual, institutional, fiduciary), likelihood rating, impact rating, risk score, mitigation measures, contingency plan, risk owner, review date, and current status. Supports program design quality, donor compliance (many donors require risk registers), and adaptive management. Versioned to track risk evolution across the program lifecycle.'
}

  end_date date [note: 'Date when this partner completed or will complete their scope of work for this intervention. May differ from the intervention\'s overall end date if partners have staggered timelines.']
  geographic_scope varchar [note: 'Specific geographic area (region, district, or community) where this partner is responsible for implementing activities within the broader intervention geography. Allows multiple partners to cover different areas of the same intervention.']
  ip_transfer_modality varchar [note: 'HACT IP transfer modality: Direct Cash Transfer / Reimbursement / Direct Payment']
  partnership_role varchar [note: 'The specific role this partner plays in the intervention (e.g., Lead Implementer, Sub-Recipient, Technical Partner, Local CBO, Consortium Member). Defines the partner\'s primary responsibility and authority level.']
  partnership_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of this specific partnership arrangement within the intervention. Tracks whether the partner is actively implementing, suspended due to performance issues, or completed their scope of work.']
  partnership_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the partnership arrangement type (e.g., Direct Implementation, Sub-Award, Technical Assistance, Capacity Building, Coordination). Determines reporting and compliance requirements.']
  performance_rating varchar [note: 'Performance assessment rating for this partner\'s work on this specific intervention. Based on delivery against milestones, budget utilization, reporting quality, and beneficiary feedback.']
  reporting_frequency varchar [note: 'Required frequency for this partner to submit progress reports for this intervention. Determined by risk rating, budget size, and donor requirements.']
  risk_rating varchar [note: 'Risk level assigned to this specific partnership based on partner capacity, geographic context, budget size, and intervention complexity. Determines oversight and monitoring intensity.']
  sector_focus varchar [note: 'Specific sector or sub-sector within the intervention that this partner is responsible for. Relevant for multi-sectoral interventions where different partners handle different technical areas (e.g., one partner for WASH, another for nutrition).']
  start_date date [note: 'Date when this partner began implementation activities for this intervention. May differ from the intervention\'s overall start date if partners were phased in.']
  sub_award_reference varchar [note: 'Unique reference number for the sub-award agreement or MoU governing this partnership. Links to legal/contractual documentation.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the formal partnership agreement between a humanitarian/development intervention and a partner organization. It captures the specific role, responsibilities, budget allocation, performance metrics, and compliance status for each partner\'s involvement in each intervention. Each record links one intervention to one partner organization with attributes that exist only in the context of this specific partnership arrangement.. Existence Justification: In nonprofit humanitarian operations, interventions are routinely implemented through multi-partner consortia where a single intervention engages multiple partner organizations (lead implementer, sub-recipients, local CBOs, technical specialists) each with distinct roles, geographic coverage, and budget allocations. Simultaneously, established partner organizations implement multiple interventions across different sectors and geographies. The partnership arrangement itself is an operational business entity that program managers actively create, monitor, and close out, with specific attributes like role, budget allocation, performance rating, compliance status, and risk assessment that belong to neither the intervention nor the partner organization alone.'
}

Table program.intervention_compliance {
  intervention_compliance_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique identifier for this intervention-specific compliance obligation record. Primary key.']
  donor_requirement_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the specific donor compliance requirement that applies to this intervention']
  intervention_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the humanitarian intervention that must fulfill this compliance requirement']
  responsible_staff_member_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the staff member assigned primary responsibility for ensuring compliance with this requirement for this specific intervention. May differ from the general staff_member_id in donor_requirement if intervention-specific ownership applies.']
  actual_effort_hours decimal(10,2) [note: 'The actual number of staff hours expended in fulfilling this compliance requirement for this specific intervention.']
  approval_date date [note: 'The date on which the donor formally approved or accepted the compliance submission for this intervention.']
  associated_cost_amount decimal(15,2) [note: 'The direct financial cost incurred to fulfill this compliance requirement for this specific intervention (e.g., audit fees, consultant costs, translation services).']
  cost_currency_code varchar [note: 'Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the associated cost amount.']
  created_date timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this intervention-compliance obligation record was created in the system.']
  deliverable_format varchar [note: 'The required format or medium for the compliance deliverable for this intervention (e.g., PDF report, Excel workbook, online portal submission).']
  due_date date [note: 'The date by which this compliance requirement must be fulfilled for this specific intervention. May differ from the general due_date in donor_requirement if intervention-specific extensions or schedules apply.']
  last_modified_date timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this intervention-compliance obligation record was last updated.']
  notes varchar [note: 'Additional free-text notes, comments, or context related to this compliance requirement for this specific intervention.']
  requirement_status varchar [note: 'Current status of compliance with this specific requirement for this specific intervention. Tracks the intervention-specific compliance state, distinct from the general requirement status in donor_requirement.']
  submission_date date [note: 'The actual date on which the compliance deliverable for this intervention was submitted to the donor.']
  waiver_granted_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the donor has approved a waiver or exemption for this compliance requirement specifically for this intervention.']
  waiver_justification varchar [note: 'The rationale or explanation provided for requesting a waiver from this compliance requirement for this specific intervention.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the compliance obligation between a humanitarian intervention and a specific donor requirement. It captures the requirement-specific compliance status, deadlines, submission tracking, and responsible staff for each intervention-requirement pair. Each record links one intervention to one donor compliance requirement with attributes that exist only in the context of this specific compliance obligation.. Existence Justification: In nonprofit grant management, a single humanitarian intervention (e.g., a WASH program) must fulfill multiple donor compliance requirements (quarterly narrative reports, financial statements, evaluations, audit submissions) imposed by one or more institutional donors funding that intervention. Conversely, a single donor compliance requirement type (e.g., quarterly narrative report format) applies to multiple interventions funded by that donor. Compliance teams actively manage each intervention-requirement pair with specific deadlines, submission tracking, approval status, responsible staff assignments, and waiver requests.'
}

Table program.component_indicator {
  component_indicator_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique identifier for this component-indicator assignment. Primary key.']
  component_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the program component being measured']
  indicator_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the MEL indicator used for measurement']
  assignment_date date [note: 'The date when this indicator was assigned to this component for monitoring. Tracks when the measurement relationship was established.']
  baseline_value decimal(18,4) [note: 'The baseline value for this indicator measured at the start of this component. Component-level baselines may differ from program-level baselines due to geographic or population differences.']
  component_indicator_status varchar [note: 'Current status of this component-indicator assignment. Indicates whether this indicator is actively being measured for this component.']
  data_collection_method varchar [note: 'The specific data collection method used for this indicator within this component (e.g., household survey, facility assessment, DHIS2 extraction, beneficiary registration). May differ from the indicator master method based on component context and available systems.']
  is_mandatory boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this indicator is mandatory for this component due to donor requirements, grant agreements, or regulatory compliance.']
  logframe_reference varchar [note: 'Reference to the specific output, outcome, or result in the component\'s LogFrame that this indicator measures. Links the indicator to the component\'s theory of change.']
  notes varchar [note: 'Free-text notes about this specific component-indicator assignment, including context, challenges, or special considerations for measurement.']
  reporting_frequency varchar [note: 'How often this indicator must be reported for this specific component. May differ from the indicator master reporting frequency based on donor requirements or component risk level.']
  responsible_unit varchar [note: 'The organizational unit, team, or field office responsible for collecting and reporting data for this indicator within this component. Assigns accountability at the component level.']
  target_value decimal(18,4) [note: 'The target value for this indicator specific to this component. May differ from the program-level or indicator master target because each component contributes differently to overall program goals.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the assignment of MEL indicators to program components for monitoring and evaluation purposes. It captures component-specific measurement targets, baselines, data collection methods, and reporting responsibilities that exist only in the context of a specific component-indicator pairing. Each record links one program component to one indicator with the specific measurement parameters for that component.. Existence Justification: In nonprofit program management, program components (e.g., WASH water supply, sanitation, hygiene promotion sub-components) are each measured by multiple MEL indicators, and indicators (especially cross-cutting ones like gender equality markers, safeguarding compliance, beneficiary satisfaction) apply across multiple components. MEL teams actively manage the component-indicator matrix in LogFrames, setting component-specific targets, baselines, and data collection methods for each pairing. This is the operational reality of results-based management in the nonprofit sector.'
}

Table program.component_system_usage {
  component_system_usage_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique identifier for this component-system usage relationship. Primary key.']
  component_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the program component that uses this system platform']
  system_platform_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the system platform used by this component']
  activation_date date [note: 'Date when this system was activated for use by this component. Tracks the start of the usage relationship. Explicitly identified in detection phase.']
  component_system_role varchar [note: 'The functional role this system plays for this specific component (e.g., Data Collection for KoboToolbox in a WASH component, Beneficiary Management for Salesforce in a cash transfer component). Explicitly identified in detection phase.']
  data_classification_level varchar [note: 'The highest data classification level of information that this component stores or processes in this specific system. May vary by component-system combination (e.g., a health component may store PII in DHIS2 while an infrastructure component stores only public data in the same system). Explicitly identified in detection phase.']
  deactivation_date date [note: 'Date when this system was deactivated or stopped being used by this component. Null if still active. Tracks the end of the usage relationship. Explicitly identified in detection phase.']

  notes varchar [note: 'Free-text notes about this component-system usage relationship, including special configurations, access restrictions, or usage patterns.']

  usage_status varchar [note: 'Current status of this component-system usage relationship (Active, Inactive, Pilot, Sunset, Decommissioned). Tracks the lifecycle of the usage relationship independently from the component or system status.']
  user_access_count varchar [note: 'Number of users from this component team who have active access to this system platform. Tracks component-specific system access provisioning. Explicitly identified in detection phase.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the operational usage relationship between program components and digital platforms. It captures which systems are actively used to deliver, monitor, or report on specific program components, including the functional role of each system, access permissions, and usage lifecycle dates. Each record links one component to one system platform with attributes that exist only in the context of this operational usage relationship.. Existence Justification: In NGO operations, program components routinely use multiple specialized digital systems simultaneously (e.g., a health component uses DHIS2 for health data, KoboToolbox for field surveys, and Salesforce for beneficiary tracking). Conversely, enterprise systems like Salesforce or DHIS2 serve multiple components across different programs and sectors. The business actively manages these usage relationships, tracking which systems support which components, provisioning access for component teams, and managing activation/deactivation as components evolve.'
}

  stage varchar [note: 'Current stage in the donor cultivation pipeline lifecycle.   wealth_screening_score decimal(5,2) [note: 'Quantitative wealth screening score from third-party wealth screening service (e.g., WealthEngine, iWave). Typically scaled 0-100 indicating relative wealth capacity.']

  pledge_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the pledge based on its purpose and structure.   reminder_schedule varchar [note: 'The timing for automated payment reminders sent to the donor before each installment due date.']

  write_off_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'The outstanding balance amount that was written off. Populated only when pledge_status is written_off.']
  write_off_date date [note: 'The date on which the pledge was written off as uncollectible. Populated only when pledge_status is written_off.']
  write_off_reason varchar [note: 'Free-text explanation for why the pledge was written off (e.g., donor deceased, donor financial hardship, unable to contact, donor dispute).']

  Note: 'Tracks multi-installment giving commitments, pledge agreements, and their individual installment schedules from donors, managed in Raisers Edge NXT and Salesforce Nonprofit Cloud. Captures pledge date, total pledge amount, installment schedule (monthly, quarterly, annual), number of installments, pledge balance outstanding, pledge status (active, fulfilled, lapsed, written-off), fund designation, campaign, appeal, reminder schedule, and write-off reason. Includes installment-level detail: individual due dates, scheduled amounts, actual payment dates, amounts paid, installment status (scheduled, paid, overdue, skipped, waived), payment method, and linked gift reference upon payment. Enables granular pledge fulfillment tracking, overdue installment identification, automated reminder generation, and BvA (Budget vs. Actual) reconciliation for pledged revenue. Distinct from gift — a pledge is a commitment to give, not a completed transaction.'
}

  Note: 'Donor segmentation master records and constituent-to-segment membership assignments used for targeted fundraising, stewardship, and communication strategies. Captures segment definition (name, type, criteria, owner, creation date, status) and constituent membership records including assignment date, assigned-by staff member, assignment source (manual, automated RFM scoring, wealth screening import), expiry date, is_active flag, and segment transition history. Segment types include giving level (major, mid-level, annual), recency-frequency-monetary (RFM) tier, donor type, geographic, programmatic interest, acquisition channel, and lifecycle stage. Enables LYBUNT (Last Year But Unfortunately Not This Year), SYBUNT, and RFM-based segmentation for direct mail, email, and major gift cultivation strategies. Supports point-in-time segment membership queries and longitudinal donor behavior analysis.'

Table donor.appeal_targeting {
  appeal_targeting_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique identifier for this appeal-segment targeting record. Primary key.']
  appeal_donor_segment_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key to the donor_segment product']
  appeal_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the fundraising appeal being deployed to this segment']
  appeal_segment_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the donor segment being targeted by this appeal']
  staff_member_id varchar [note: 'Identifier of the staff member who created this targeting assignment.']
  average_gift_amount decimal(15,2) [note: 'Average gift size for responses from this segment to this appeal, calculated as total_revenue_amount / response_count. Used to compare segment giving capacity.']
  cost_allocated decimal(15,2) [note: 'Portion of the total appeal cost allocated to this segment based on pieces sent or other cost allocation methodology. Enables segment-level ROI calculation.']
  cost_currency_code varchar [note: 'Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the allocated cost amount.']
  created_date timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this appeal-segment targeting record was created in the system.']
  deployment_date date [note: 'Date when the appeal was deployed to this specific segment. May differ from overall appeal mailing_date if segments are deployed in waves.']
  last_updated_date timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when performance metrics for this appeal-segment combination were last updated.']
  pieces_sent varchar [note: 'Number of solicitation pieces (letters, emails, calls) sent specifically to constituents in this segment for this appeal. This is segment-specific volume tracking.']
  response_count varchar [note: 'Number of constituents from this segment who responded to this appeal with a gift or pledge. Enables segment-level response analysis.']
  response_rate_percent decimal(5,2) [note: 'Response rate percentage for this specific appeal-segment combination, calculated as (response_count / pieces_sent) * 100. Critical metric for segment performance evaluation.']
  revenue_currency_code decimal(18,2) [note: 'Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the segment revenue amount (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP).']
  roi_ratio decimal(10,4) [note: 'Return on investment ratio for this appeal-segment combination, calculated as total_revenue_amount / cost_allocated. Critical metric for optimizing future segment targeting decisions.']
  segment_ask_amount decimal(15,2) [note: 'Suggested gift amount presented to constituents in this segment, which may differ from the general appeal ask_amount based on segment giving capacity (e.g., major donors receive higher asks).']
  target_segment varchar [note: 'Description of the constituent segment targeted by this appeal (e.g., lapsed donors 12-24 months, major gift prospects $10K+, monthly sustainers). [Moved from appeal: The target_segment STRING attribute in appeal is a text description that cannot capture the reality of multi-segment targeting. When an appeal targets multiple segments (e.g., \'Major Donors\', \'LYBUNT Q1\', \'Mid-Level Annual\'), this single STRING field would require concatenation or comma-separated values, making it impossible to query segment-specific performance. This attribute should be removed from appeal as the relationship is now properly modeled through the appeal_targeting association.]']
  test_variant varchar [note: 'Identifier for A/B test variant or creative package version used for this segment (e.g., \'Control\', \'Variant_A\', \'High_Ask\'). Enables multivariate testing across segments.']
  total_revenue_amount decimal(15,2) [note: 'Total gross revenue generated by gifts and pledges from this segment in response to this appeal. Enables segment-level revenue attribution and ROI calculation.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the targeting relationship between fundraising appeals and donor segments. It captures the operational execution of multi-segment direct marketing campaigns where a single appeal is deployed to multiple constituent segments with segment-specific performance tracking. Each record links one appeal to one donor segment with attributes that measure the effectiveness of that specific appeal-segment combination including pieces sent, response metrics, revenue attribution, and ROI analysis.. Existence Justification: In nonprofit fundraising operations, appeals routinely target multiple donor segments simultaneously with segment-specific execution parameters (different ask amounts for major vs. annual donors, different creative variants for A/B testing, wave-based deployment schedules). Each appeal-segment combination generates its own performance metrics (pieces sent, response rate, revenue, ROI) that fundraisers actively analyze to optimize future targeting decisions. This is not a theoretical correlation but an operational business process where development teams create targeting plans, execute multi-segment campaigns, and measure segment-level results.'
}

Table donor.event_registration {
  event_registration_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique identifier for this event registration record. Primary key.']
  constituent_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the constituent who registered for or attended the fundraising event']
  fundraising_event_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the fundraising event for which the constituent registered']
  attendance_status varchar [note: 'The current status of the constituent\'s attendance (registered, confirmed, checked_in, no_show, cancelled). Tracks the registration lifecycle from initial signup through event day check-in. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.']
  auction_paddle_number varchar [note: 'The paddle or bidder number assigned to the constituent for auction participation at the event. Links to auction transaction tracking. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.']
  check_in_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The precise date and time when the constituent checked in at the event. Used to confirm actual attendance and trigger post-event stewardship workflows.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when this registration record was created in the system.']
  dietary_restrictions varchar [note: 'Any dietary restrictions or meal preferences specified by the constituent during registration (vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free, allergies). Used for catering planning. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.']
  guest_count varchar [note: 'The number of guests included in this registration (e.g., table sponsorships may include multiple seats). Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.']
  last_modified_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when this registration record was last updated.']
  payment_method decimal(18,2) [note: 'The method of payment used for the registration (credit card, check, cash, wire transfer, complimentary). Supports reconciliation and revenue tracking.']
  payment_status decimal(18,2) [note: 'The current payment status for this registration (paid, pending, refunded, waived). Tracks financial completion of the registration.']
  post_event_follow_up_status varchar [note: 'The status of post-event stewardship and cultivation follow-up activities for this constituent (pending, thank_you_sent, survey_sent, completed). Tracks donor engagement workflow completion.']
  registration_date date [note: 'The date on which the constituent registered for the fundraising event. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.']
  registration_source varchar [note: 'The channel through which the constituent registered for the event (online, phone, mail, in-person, staff entry). Used for marketing effectiveness analysis.']
  registration_type varchar [note: 'The type of registration or participation role for this constituent at the event (attendee, table sponsor, individual sponsor, volunteer). Determines engagement level and stewardship approach.']
  special_requests varchar [note: 'Any special requests or accommodations requested by the constituent (accessibility needs, seating preferences, VIP treatment). Used for event logistics and donor stewardship.']
  table_number varchar [note: 'The table number or seating assignment for the constituent at the event. Used for seating logistics and VIP placement. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data (table_assignment/table_number).']
  ticket_price_paid decimal(18,2) [note: 'The actual amount paid by the constituent for their ticket or registration. May differ from standard ticket price due to discounts, early bird pricing, or sponsorship levels. Corresponds to amount_paid in detection phase data.']
  ticket_type varchar [note: 'The specific ticket tier or type purchased by the constituent (e.g., general admission, VIP, early bird). Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the registration and attendance relationship between constituents and fundraising events. It captures the complete lifecycle of constituent participation in donor cultivation and fundraising activities, from initial registration through post-event follow-up. Each record links one constituent to one fundraising event with transactional attributes including registration details, ticketing information, seating assignments, payment tracking, attendance confirmation, and stewardship workflow status. This is a core operational entity managed actively by development and events staff for capacity planning, revenue tracking, donor engagement measurement, and post-event cultivation workflows.. Existence Justification: In nonprofit fundraising operations, constituents register for and attend multiple fundraising events over their donor lifecycle (galas, golf tournaments, cultivation dinners), and each event hosts multiple constituent attendees. Event registration is an actively managed operational process with its own lifecycle: registration → payment → seating assignment → check-in → post-event follow-up. This is distinct from gift processing—not all attendees make gifts, and registration data (ticket type, table assignment, dietary restrictions, attendance confirmation) is managed separately from donation transactions.'
}

Table donor.participation {
  participation_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique identifier for this participation record. Primary key.']
  campaign_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the campaign in which the constituent participated']
  constituent_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the constituent who participated in the campaign']
  staff_member_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the staff member who solicited or engaged this constituent for this campaign. Enables tracking of fundraiser effectiveness.']
  acknowledgment_sent_date date [note: 'The date when acknowledgment communication was sent to the constituent for this participation. Null if not yet sent.']
  acknowledgment_sent_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a thank-you or acknowledgment communication was sent to the constituent for this participation. Used for stewardship tracking.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this participation record was first created in the system.']
  gift_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'The monetary amount contributed by the constituent to this campaign in this participation instance. Null if participation type is not gift. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.']
  participation_date date [note: 'The date when this participation event occurred. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.']
  participation_type varchar [note: 'The type of participation or engagement activity. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data. Values include solicitation (outreach attempt), gift (monetary contribution), pledge (commitment to give), volunteer (time contribution), advocacy (campaign promotion), event_attendance (campaign event participation), non_response (solicited but did not respond).']
  pledge_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'The monetary amount pledged by the constituent to this campaign in this participation instance. Null if participation type is not pledge. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.']
  response_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the constituent responded to the campaign solicitation. True = responded (gift, pledge, volunteer, etc.); False = solicited but no response. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.']
  solicitation_channel varchar [note: 'The communication channel through which the constituent was solicited or engaged for this campaign. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this participation record was last modified.']
  volunteer_hours decimal(8,2) [note: 'The number of hours the constituent volunteered for this campaign in this participation instance. Null if participation type is not volunteer. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the participation event between constituent and campaign. It captures every instance of constituent engagement with a fundraising campaign, including solicitation attempts, responses, gifts, pledges, volunteer activities, and advocacy actions. Each record links one constituent to one campaign with attributes that exist only in the context of this specific engagement instance.. Existence Justification: In nonprofit fundraising operations, constituents participate in multiple campaigns over time (annual fund, emergency appeals, capital campaigns, etc.), and each campaign engages multiple constituents through various solicitation channels. Campaign participation is a recognized business concept that fundraising teams actively manage, track, and analyze. The relationship carries rich operational data including participation type, solicitation channel, response outcomes, gift/pledge amounts, and volunteer hours that belong to neither the constituent nor the campaign alone but to each specific engagement instance.'
}

Table donor.segment_membership {
  segment_membership_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique identifier for this segment membership record. Primary key.']
  constituent_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the constituent who is a member of this donor segment']
  primary_donor_segment_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key to donor_segment. Part of the many-to-many relationship.']

  assignment_source varchar [note: 'Source system or process that created this membership record (e.g., \'Salesforce NPSP\', \'Raiser\'s Edge NXT\', \'RFM Batch Job\', \'Manual Entry\'). Referenced in Product B description.']

  frequency_count varchar [note: 'Number of gifts in the scoring window (RFM frequency).']

  is_manual_override boolean [note: 'Whether this segment membership was manually overridden by staff.']
  last_modified_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this segment membership record was last updated.']
  lifetime_giving_at_assignment timestamp [note: 'Lifetime giving amount of the constituent at the time of segment assignment.']
  membership_end_date date [note: 'Date when the constituent membership in this segment ended or expired. Null for active memberships. Explicitly identified in detection reasoning as relationship data.']
  membership_start_date date [note: 'Date when the constituent was assigned to this donor segment. Explicitly identified in detection reasoning as relationship data.']
  membership_status varchar [note: 'Current status of the segment membership.']
  monetary_value decimal(18,2) [note: 'Total monetary value in the scoring window (RFM monetary).']
  next_review_date date [note: 'Date when this segment membership is next scheduled for review.']
  override_reason varchar [note: 'Reason for manual override of segment assignment if applicable.']
  recency_days varchar [note: 'Number of days since last gift at the time of segment assignment (RFM recency).']
  removal_reason varchar [note: 'Reason the constituent was removed from the segment.']
  score_at_assignment varchar [note: 'RFM score, wealth rating, or other quantitative score that qualified the constituent for this segment at the time of assignment. Explicitly identified in detection reasoning as relationship data.']
  score_at_reassessment timestamp [note: 'Segment score at most recent reassessment.']
  segment_assignment_reason varchar [note: 'Business rationale or rule that triggered this segment assignment (e.g., \'Total giving >$10K in FY2024\', \'LYBUNT - gave $5K in 2023, $0 in 2024\', \'Wealth screening capacity $100K+\'). Explicitly identified in detection reasoning as relationship data.']
  source_system_code varchar [note: 'Source system that generated the membership record.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the membership relationship between constituents and donor segments. It captures the assignment of constituents to fundraising and stewardship segments for targeted communication, cultivation, and reporting. Each record links one constituent to one donor segment with temporal, attribution, and scoring attributes that exist only in the context of this specific membership assignment.. Existence Justification: Constituent segmentation is a core operational fundraising process where nonprofits actively manage multi-dimensional segment assignments. Constituents simultaneously belong to multiple segments (e.g., a major donor can be in \'Major Donors 2024\', \'LYBUNT Q1\', \'East Coast Region\', and \'Health Program Interest\' at the same time), and each segment contains many constituents. The business manages segment membership as a distinct lifecycle with assignment rules, temporal tracking, scoring attribution, and transition history for targeted cultivation, stewardship, and campaign execution.'
}

  reporting_frequency varchar [note: 'How often this donor requires progress reporting specifically for this indicator. May differ from the indicator\'s standard reporting frequency due to donor-specific requirements.']
  restriction_type varchar [note: 'The type of restriction the donor has placed on this indicator funding. Unrestricted = no restrictions; Restricted = tied to specific activities/geographies; Temporarily Restricted = time-bound restrictions; Permanently Restricted = endowment-style restrictions; Earmarked = donor-specified use.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the funding relationship between a constituent (donor/funder) and a specific MEL indicator. It captures donor-specific funding allocations, restrictions, targets, and reporting requirements for individual indicators across programs and grants. Each record links one constituent to one indicator with funding terms, amounts, timeframes, and performance targets that exist only in the context of this donor-indicator funding relationship. Essential for donor-specific impact reporting, compliance with funder restrictions, and tracking indicator-level funding sources.. Existence Justification: In nonprofit operations, donors (bilateral agencies like USAID/DFID, multilateral organizations, foundations) fund specific MEL indicators across multiple programs and grants, and each indicator receives funding from multiple donor sources. The business actively manages these donor-indicator funding relationships with specific funding amounts, timeframes, restrictions (unrestricted vs. earmarked), donor-specific targets, and reporting frequencies that differ by donor. This is a recognized operational concept called \'Donor Indicator Funding\' or \'Indicator-Level Funding Allocation\' that program managers and MEL officers actively create, track, and report on for donor compliance and impact reporting.'
}

  sample_size_planned varchar [note: 'The planned number of beneficiary households or individuals to be surveyed as part of the PDM sample design.']
  sampling_method varchar [note: 'The statistical sampling approach used to select beneficiaries for the PDM survey to ensure representativeness and validity of findings.']
  satisfaction_score decimal(3,2) [note: 'Overall beneficiary satisfaction score (typically 0.00 to 5.00 scale) with the distribution process, item quality, and timeliness. Core accountability metric per CHS Commitment 4.']
  sdg_alignment varchar [note: 'Sustainable Development Goal(s) that the distribution and PDM survey contribute to, supporting organizational impact reporting and strategic alignment.']
  survey_code varchar [note: 'Externally-known unique business identifier for the PDM survey, typically following organizational naming conventions for tracking and reporting purposes.']
  survey_date date [note: 'The principal date when the PDM survey field data collection was conducted or completed. Represents the business event timestamp for accountability reporting.']
  survey_end_date date [note: 'Date when the PDM survey field data collection activities were completed.']
  survey_methodology varchar [note: 'The primary data collection methodology employed for this PDM survey, such as household interviews, FGD (Focus Group Discussion), KII (Key Informant Interview), or mobile data collection via KoboToolbox.']
  survey_start_date date [note: 'Date when the PDM survey field data collection activities commenced.']
  survey_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the PDM survey indicating its progress through planning, field data collection, analysis, and approval stages.']
  surveyor_organization varchar [note: 'Name of the organization (implementing partner, third-party evaluator, or internal MEL team) that conducted the PDM survey.']
  utilization_rate_percent decimal(5,2) [note: 'Percentage of surveyed beneficiaries who reported using or consuming the distributed items as intended. Key indicator of distribution appropriateness and effectiveness.']
  vulnerability_disaggregation_available boolean [note: 'Flag indicating whether the PDM survey data includes disaggregation by vulnerability status (e.g., persons with disabilities, elderly, female-headed households) for equity analysis.']

  Note: 'Transactional record of a Post-Distribution Monitoring (PDM) survey conducted after a distribution event to assess appropriateness, adequacy, and utilization of distributed items. Captures survey date, linked distribution event, sample size, survey methodology, key findings (utilization rate, adequacy score, complaints received, protection concerns noted), and recommendations. Supports accountability to affected populations (AAP) and CHS compliance.'
}

  participation_date date [note: 'The date this volunteer participated in the assessment fieldwork. May differ from assessment_date if the assessment spanned multiple days and this volunteer only participated on specific days. Supports attendance tracking and per-diem calculation.']
  participation_status varchar [note: 'Current status of this volunteer\'s participation in this assessment. Tracks lifecycle from recruitment through completion.   quality_review_status varchar [note: 'Status of the quality review for this participation record (e.g., pending, approved, flagged).']
  refusal_count varchar [note: 'Number of respondents who refused to participate during this session.']
  respondent_type varchar [note: 'Category of respondent (e.g., head of household, community leader, key informant).']
  security_clearance_status varchar [note: 'Security clearance status of the enumerator for the assessment area.']
  supervision_notes varchar [note: 'Notes from the supervisor regarding this participant\'s performance.']
  surveys_completed_count varchar [note: 'Number of individual survey submissions, interviews, or FGD sessions this volunteer completed during this assessment. Used for productivity tracking, workload balancing, and incentive calculation. This is assessment-specific—cannot be stored on volunteer (varies by assessment) or assessment (varies by volunteer).']
  training_completion_status varchar [note: 'Status indicating whether this volunteer completed the methodology-specific training required for this assessment (e.g., MUAC screening training, PDM interview protocol, KoboToolbox form training). Values: completed (training done), not_required (volunteer already certified), pending (scheduled), incomplete (did not complete). This is assessment-specific because different assessment types require different training.']
  travel_time_minutes varchar [note: 'Time in minutes the enumerator traveled to reach the assessment site.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this participation record was last updated.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the participation relationship between field assessments and volunteers who serve as enumerators or team members. It captures the operational reality that assessments are conducted by multi-person teams, and volunteers participate in multiple assessments over time. Each record links one assessment to one volunteer with attributes that exist only in the context of this specific participation: the volunteer\'s role in that assessment, their performance metrics, and training completion status for that particular assessment methodology.. Existence Justification: In nonprofit field operations, assessments (FGDs, KIIs, household surveys, PDM, MUAC screening) are conducted by multi-person enumerator teams, and volunteers participate in multiple assessments over time across different projects and methodologies. The business actively manages assessment participation as an operational entity: field coordinators recruit volunteers for specific assessments, assign roles (lead vs. enumerator), track data quality scores per volunteer per assessment, verify methodology-specific training completion, and use this data for volunteer performance management and future assignment decisions.'
}

Essential for procurement audit trails, competitive bidding transparency, and donor compliance reporting per 2 CFR 200 procurement standards.. Existence Justification: In humanitarian procurement operations, RFQs are issued to multiple vendors during competitive bidding processes, and each vendor submits a formal bid with pricing, technical proposals, and delivery terms. The business actively manages each bid submission through evaluation scoring, ranking, and award decisions. This is not a simple reference but an operational business entity that procurement officers create, evaluate, and audit for donor compliance per 2 CFR 200 standards.'

  assessment_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the capacity assessment record: DRAFT (initiated but not submitted), IN_PROGRESS (assessment underway), COMPLETED (assessment finalized), VALIDATED (reviewed and approved by authorized staff), ARCHIVED (superseded or closed).']
  assessment_tool_version varchar [note: 'Version number or edition of the assessment methodology tool used (e.g., \'USAID OCA v3.0\', \'DFID OCAT 2019\'). Ensures comparability of scores across assessments conducted using different tool versions.']
  assessment_type varchar [note: 'Classification of when and why the assessment was conducted: PRE_AWARD (due diligence before partnership), PERIODIC (scheduled review during partnership), TRIGGERED (event-driven reassessment due to risk flag), or CLOSE_OUT (end-of-partnership evaluation).']
  capacity_assessment_code varchar
  capacity_assessment_description varchar
  capacity_assessment_name varchar
  capacity_assessment_status varchar
  capacity_building_plan_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the assessment results mandate the development of a formal capacity-building plan (True) or whether the partner\'s capacity is sufficient without a structured intervention plan (False).']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp indicating when the capacity assessment record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail, data lineage, and compliance reporting purposes.']
  end_date date
  enhanced_monitoring_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the assessment outcome requires enhanced programmatic or financial monitoring of the partner (True), such as more frequent reporting, additional site visits, or pre-approval of expenditures, as mandated by donor regulations.']
  financial_mgmt_score decimal(5,2) [note: 'Numeric score assigned to the partner\'s financial management functional area, covering accounting systems, internal controls, audit compliance, and fund stewardship. Typically scored on a 0–100 or 1–5 scale per the assessment methodology.']
  financial_risk_rating varchar [note: 'Specific risk rating for the partner\'s financial management functional area, used to determine sub-award monitoring intensity, payment modality, and required financial controls.']
  governance_score decimal(5,2) [note: 'Numeric score for the partner\'s organizational governance functional area, including board oversight, legal registration, organizational policies, and leadership accountability.']
  hr_mgmt_score decimal(5,2) [note: 'Numeric score for the partner\'s human resources management functional area, including HR policies, recruitment practices, staff development, and safeguarding compliance.']
  it_systems_score decimal(5,2) [note: 'Numeric score for the partner\'s ICT4D and information systems functional area, covering data management infrastructure, cybersecurity practices, and digital reporting capabilities.']
  key_findings_summary varchar [note: 'Concise narrative summary of the principal findings from the capacity assessment, highlighting major strengths, critical gaps, and priority areas for improvement across all assessed functional areas.']
  kobo_submission_reference varchar [note: 'Unique submission identifier from KoboToolbox or similar field data collection platform used to capture assessment data in the field. Enables traceability back to the source data collection record.']
  lead_assessor_name varchar [note: 'Full name of the individual who led the capacity assessment. Retained for reporting and audit purposes even when the staff record may change.']
  lead_assessor_organization varchar [note: 'Name of the organization to which the lead assessor belongs (e.g., the NGO\'s headquarters, an independent consulting firm, or a donor agency). Relevant when external assessors are engaged.']
  mel_score decimal(5,2) [note: 'Numeric score for the partner\'s Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning (MEL) functional area, covering data collection systems, indicator tracking, reporting quality, and learning practices.']
  modified_timestamp timestamp
  next_assessment_due_date date [note: 'Scheduled date by which the next capacity assessment must be completed, based on risk rating, donor requirements, or organizational policy. Drives compliance monitoring and workflow triggers.']
  notes varchar
  overall_risk_rating varchar [note: 'Categorical risk classification assigned to the partner based on the capacity assessment results: LOW (strong capacity, minimal oversight needed), MEDIUM (adequate capacity with some gaps), HIGH (significant capacity gaps requiring intensive support), CRITICAL (fundamental weaknesses posing fiduciary or programmatic risk).']
  overall_score decimal(5,2) [note: 'Composite numeric score representing the partner\'s overall organizational capacity across all assessed functional areas. Calculated per the assessment methodology\'s weighting scheme and recorded as the official assessment result.']
  partner_self_assessment_completed boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the partner organization completed a self-assessment component prior to or alongside the external assessment (True). Many OCA methodologies include a parallel self-assessment to identify perception gaps.']
  partner_self_assessment_score decimal(5,2) [note: 'Overall score submitted by the partner organization in their self-assessment component. Compared against the external assessor\'s score to identify perception gaps and inform capacity-building dialogue.']
  payment_modality_recommendation decimal(18,2) [note: 'Payment modality recommended for sub-award disbursements based on the partner\'s financial risk rating: ADVANCE (funds transferred before expenditure), REIMBURSEMENT (funds transferred after expenditure documentation), DIRECT_PAYMENT (NGO pays vendors directly on partner\'s behalf), MIXED (combination of modalities).']
  procurement_score decimal(5,2) [note: 'Numeric score for the partner\'s procurement and supply chain management functional area, covering procurement policies, competitive bidding, vendor management, and asset control.']
  program_mgmt_score decimal(5,2) [note: 'Numeric score for the partner\'s program design and management functional area, including project planning, implementation capacity, beneficiary targeting, and service delivery quality.']
  recommended_interventions varchar [note: 'Narrative description of the specific capacity-building interventions recommended based on assessment findings, such as financial management training, procurement system upgrades, MEL system strengthening, or governance policy development.']
  score_scale_max decimal(5,2) [note: 'The maximum possible score on the scoring scale used by the assessment methodology (e.g., 100 for percentage-based scales, 5 for Likert-based scales). Required to normalize scores across different methodologies for comparative analytics.']
  start_date date
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp indicating when the capacity assessment record was most recently modified. Used for change tracking, data synchronization, and audit trail purposes.']
  validation_date date [note: 'Date on which the capacity assessment was formally reviewed and validated by the authorized staff member, marking the record as officially approved for use in partnership and sub-award decisions.']

  Note: 'Partner capacity assessment including HACT micro-assessment. Source systems: eTools, eZHACT, UN Partner Portal.'
}

Due diligence incorporates capacit']

Links DD workflow to compliance evide']

Pre-award is conducted before sub-award execution; periodic review is scheduled; triggered review is initiated by a risk event; close-out is conducted at agreement end; enhanced due diligence applies to high-risk partners.']

  due_diligence_record_name varchar
  due_diligence_record_status varchar
  end_date date
  financial_audit_opinion varchar [note: 'Type of auditor\'s opinion issued in the partner\'s most recent external financial audit. An unqualified (clean) opinion is required for most donor sub-award eligibility. Adverse or disclaimer opinions trigger enhanced due diligence.']

Null if no ISO certification is held. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: ISO_9001|ISO_27001|ISO_14001|ISO_45001|ISO_31000|none — promote to reference product]']

  legal_registration_verified boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the partner\'s legal registration and incorporation status in its country of operation has been verified against official national NGO registration records or company registry.']
  modified_timestamp timestamp

  notes varchar
  overall_outcome varchar [note: 'Final determination of the due diligence exercise indicating whether the partner is cleared for sub-award or partnership engagement. Approved with conditions requires a documented corrective action plan.']
  record_reference_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known unique alphanumeric reference code assigned to this due diligence record, used in correspondence, audit trails, and donor reporting. Format: DDR-YYYY-NNNNNN.']
  reviewer_notes varchar [note: 'Confidential narrative notes recorded by the responsible staff member summarizing key findings, concerns, and recommendations from the due diligence review. Restricted to compliance and partnership leadership.']
  risk_level varchar [note: 'Composite risk rating assigned to the partner following due diligence, reflecting financial, governance, compliance, and operational risk factors. Determines monitoring intensity and sub-award conditions.']
  risk_score varchar [note: 'Numeric composite risk score (typically 0–100) calculated from weighted assessment criteria across financial, governance, legal, and operational dimensions. Supports quantitative risk ranking across the partner portfolio.']
  safeguarding_policy_verified boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the partner has a documented and operational safeguarding policy covering protection from sexual exploitation, abuse, and harassment (PSEAH), child protection, and GBV prevention, as required by IASC and donor standards.']
  sphere_compliance_status varchar [note: 'Assessment of the partner\'s operational compliance with the Sphere Humanitarian Charter and Minimum Standards in Humanitarian Response, covering WASH, food security, shelter, and health sectors.']
  start_date date
  supporting_document_ref varchar [note: 'Reference identifier or URL pointing to the document management system location where supporting due diligence evidence (audit reports, registration certificates, signed certifications) is stored.']

  Note: 'Formal due diligence and partner verification master record covering legal compliance checks, sanctions screening (OFAC, EU, UN), anti-terrorism certification, financial audit review, governance verification, and regulatory standing. Includes embedded accreditation/certification tracking for CHS (Core Humanitarian Standard), Sphere compliance, HAP membership, ISO certifications, and national NGO registration status with issuing body, certificate number, issue date, expiry date, and verification status. Tracks due diligence type, completion date, outcome, risk level, next review date, and responsible staff. Required for compliance with 2 CFR 200, USAID ADS 303, and donor partner vetting regulations. This is the SSOT for all partner verification, screening, and accreditation data in the partnership domain.'
}

Table partnership.agreement_amendment {
  agreement_amendment_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique system-generated identifier for each formal modification record to a partnership agreement. Serves as the primary key for the agreement_amendment entity.']
  partnership_agreement_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the parent partnership agreement (MoU, LoA, SoW, or sub-award) that this amendment modifies. Links the amendment to its originating agreement record.']

  agreement_amendment_code varchar
  agreement_amendment_description varchar
  agreement_amendment_name varchar

  amendment_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known sequential identifier for this amendment within the context of the parent agreement (e.g., AMD-2024-001). Used in official correspondence, donor reporting, and compliance filings. Supports full amendment history tracking per agreement.']
  amendment_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the amendment record. Draft indicates preparation in progress; pending_approval indicates submission to approval authority; approved indicates fully executed; rejected indicates declined by approver; superseded indicates replaced by a subsequent amendment; withdrawn indicates retracted before approval.']
  amendment_title varchar [note: 'Short descriptive title summarizing the purpose of the amendment (e.g., \'No-Cost Extension to December 2025\', \'Budget Realignment Q3 2024\'). Used in correspondence, dashboards, and partner communications.']
  amendment_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the formal modification being made to the agreement. Scope change alters deliverables or geographic coverage; budget realignment redistributes funds across cost categories; no-cost extension extends the period without additional funding; period of performance adjusts start/end dates; signatory change updates authorized representatives. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: scope_change|budget_realignment|no_cost_extension|period_of_performance|signatory_change|other — promote to reference product]']
  approval_authority varchar [note: 'Name or title of the individual, committee, or organizational body with delegated authority to approve this amendment (e.g., Country Director, Grants Manager, Donor Agreement Officer). Supports RACI accountability tracking.']
  approved_date date [note: 'The date on which the amendment was formally approved by the designated approval authority. Null if not yet approved or if rejected/withdrawn.']
  beneficiary_target_change boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this amendment modifies the target beneficiary numbers, population groups, or vulnerability criteria for the program. True = beneficiary targets modified; False = no change. Relevant for MEL/MEAL reporting and SDG indicator tracking.']
  budget_change_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'The net monetary change to the agreement budget introduced by this amendment (revised_budget_amount minus original_budget_amount). Positive values indicate budget increases; negative values indicate reductions. Null for non-financial amendments.']
  clauses_modified varchar [note: 'Enumeration or description of the specific agreement clauses, articles, or sections that are modified by this amendment (e.g., \'Article 3 — Scope of Work, Article 7 — Budget\'). Supports legal review and compliance tracking.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'System timestamp recording when this amendment record was first created in the data platform. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and compliance with record-keeping requirements under 2 CFR 200 and FASB ASC 958.']
  currency_code varchar [note: 'ISO 4217 three-letter currency code applicable to all monetary amounts in this amendment record (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Ensures consistent financial reporting across multi-currency partnership portfolios.']
  document_reference varchar [note: 'File path, document management system reference, or URL pointing to the executed amendment document (signed PDF or equivalent). Supports audit trail and compliance evidence requirements.']
  donor_approval_reference varchar [note: 'Reference number, letter identifier, or correspondence tracking code for the donor\'s written prior approval of this amendment. Required for audit evidence when donor_prior_approval_required is True.']
  donor_prior_approval_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this amendment requires prior written approval from the donor or prime recipient before implementation, as mandated under 2 CFR 200.308 or specific award terms. True = prior approval required; False = notification only or no approval needed.']
  effective_date date [note: 'The date on which the amendment becomes legally binding and operationally effective. This is the real-world event date, distinct from the signature date or record creation timestamp. Critical for period-of-performance tracking and financial reporting.']
  end_date date
  execution_date date [note: 'The date on which all required signatories formally signed and executed the amendment document. May differ from the effective date when retroactive amendments are issued.']
  extension_duration_days varchar [note: 'Number of calendar days by which the period of performance is extended by this amendment. Null for non-extension amendments. Used for program planning, resource allocation, and donor reporting on timeline changes.']
  geographic_scope_change boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this amendment modifies the geographic coverage or operational areas of the agreement (e.g., adding or removing districts, countries, or OCHA cluster areas). True = geographic scope modified; False = no geographic change.']
  gms_reference varchar [note: 'External reference identifier for this amendment as recorded in the Grant Management System (GMS) or donor\'s award management platform (e.g., USAID ASIST, DFID ARIES). Enables cross-system reconciliation and donor audit support.']
  iati_activity_identifier varchar [note: 'IATI-standard activity identifier associated with the parent agreement, used to publish amendment data to the IATI Registry for transparency and open data compliance. Format follows IATI hierarchical identifier standard.']
  is_no_cost_extension boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this amendment constitutes a no-cost extension (NCE), extending the period of performance without additional funding. True = NCE; False = other amendment type. Critical for grant closeout planning and donor reporting.']
  justification varchar [note: 'Narrative explanation of the business rationale for the amendment, including the circumstances that necessitated the change (e.g., context changes, operational constraints, donor-directed modifications). Required for donor reporting and audit compliance under 2 CFR 200.']
  modified_timestamp timestamp
  ngo_signatory_name varchar [note: 'Full name of the authorized representative of Ngo who signs this amendment on behalf of the organization. Required for legal enforceability and signatory change tracking.']
  notes varchar [note: 'Free-text field for additional context, internal commentary, or operational notes related to this amendment that do not fit structured fields. Used by grants management and partnership teams for internal coordination.']
  original_budget_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'The total authorized budget of the agreement prior to this amendment, expressed in the agreement currency. Retained for Budget versus Actual (BvA) analysis and audit trail of financial modifications.']
  original_end_date date [note: 'The end date of the period of performance as defined in the agreement prior to this amendment. Used to calculate extension duration and track no-cost extension history.']
  original_start_date date [note: 'The start date of the period of performance as defined in the agreement prior to this amendment. Retained for audit trail and comparison purposes when a period-of-performance amendment is processed.']
  partner_signatory_name varchar [note: 'Full name of the authorized representative of the partner organization who signs this amendment on behalf of the CSO, CBO, INGO, government body, or UN agency. Required for signatory change amendments and legal enforceability.']
  revised_beneficiary_target varchar [note: 'Updated total number of direct beneficiaries targeted under the agreement following this amendment. Null if beneficiary_target_change is False. Used for MEL/MEAL indicator tracking and donor results reporting.']
  revised_budget_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'The total authorized budget of the agreement as updated by this amendment. Null if this amendment does not modify the budget. Used for BvA reporting and donor financial compliance.']
  revised_end_date date [note: 'The updated end date of the period of performance as established by this amendment. Null if this amendment does not modify the end date. Key field for no-cost extension tracking.']
  revised_start_date date [note: 'The updated start date of the period of performance as established by this amendment. Null if this amendment does not modify the start date.']
  scope_change_description varchar [note: 'Detailed narrative describing changes to the Scope of Work (SoW), program activities, geographic coverage, target beneficiary populations, or deliverables introduced by this amendment. Null if amendment type is not scope_change.']
  start_date date
  submitted_date date [note: 'The date on which the amendment request was formally submitted to the approval authority or donor/prime for review. Used to track processing timelines and compliance with advance notification requirements under 2 CFR 200.']

  Note: 'Transactional record capturing formal modifications to existing partnership agreements including scope changes, budget realignments, no-cost extensions, period of performance adjustments, and signatory changes.
