  follow_up_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a follow-up visit, mentoring session, or technical assistance is required after this activity to reinforce learning or address outstanding gaps. Drives scheduling of subsequent capacity-building activities.']
  is_certified boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a certificate of completion or competency was issued to participants upon successful completion of this capacity-building activity. Relevant for accredited training programs and professional development tracking.']
  last_updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this capacity-building activity record was most recently modified. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER RECORD_AUDIT_UPDATED category. Used for data lineage, audit trails, and incremental ETL processing. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.']
  linked_capacity_gap varchar [note: 'Description or reference code of the specific capacity gap identified in the partner\'s capacity assessment that this activity is designed to address. Enables traceability from gap identification to intervention delivery.']
  location_name varchar [note: 'Name of the specific city, district, or venue where the capacity-building activity took place (e.g., \'Nairobi Regional Office\', \'Kampala Training Centre\'). Complements country code for field-level geographic reporting.']
  male_participants varchar [note: 'Number of male participants in this capacity-building activity. Required for gender disaggregation reporting per USAID Gender Equality Policy and SDG 5 indicators.']
  materials_provided boolean [note: 'Indicates whether training materials, toolkits, manuals, or job aids were distributed to participants as part of this capacity-building activity. Relevant for resource tracking and follow-up support planning.']
  modified_timestamp timestamp
  notes varchar [note: 'Free-text field for capturing qualitative observations, lessons learned, contextual factors, or any other relevant information about the capacity-building activity not captured in structured fields. Supports MEL narrative reporting.']
  participant_satisfaction_score decimal(4,2) [note: 'Average satisfaction rating provided by participants in post-activity feedback forms, typically on a scale of 1–5 or 1–10. Used for activity quality improvement and facilitator performance assessment.']
  post_assessment_score decimal(5,2) [note: 'Average knowledge or competency assessment score recorded for participants after the capacity-building activity concluded. Compared against pre-assessment score to measure learning gain and activity effectiveness.']
  pre_assessment_score decimal(5,2) [note: 'Average knowledge or competency assessment score recorded for participants before the capacity-building activity commenced. Used to establish a baseline for measuring learning gain. Expressed as a percentage (0–100). Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER QUANTITATIVE_RESULT category (non-monetary).']
  scheduled_end_date date [note: 'Planned date on which the capacity-building activity was originally scheduled to conclude. Used for duration planning and workplan management.']
  scheduled_start_date date [note: 'Planned date on which the capacity-building activity was originally scheduled to begin. Used for planning, calendar management, and variance analysis against actual delivery.']
  start_date date
  thematic_area varchar [note: 'Primary thematic or sectoral focus of the capacity-building activity (e.g., \'Financial Management\', \'MEAL\', \'WASH\', \'GBV Prevention\', \'Procurement\', \'Safeguarding\', \'Proposal Writing\'). Used for portfolio analysis and gap identification. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: financial_management|meal|wash|gbv_prevention|procurement|safeguarding|proposal_writing|hr_management|logistics|governance — promote to reference product]']
  topics_covered varchar [note: 'Free-text or structured description of the specific topics, modules, or competencies addressed during the activity (e.g., \'Budget vs Actual reporting, SAP navigation, donor compliance rules\'). Supports curriculum documentation and knowledge management.']
  total_participants varchar [note: 'Total number of individuals from the partner organization who participated in this capacity-building activity. Core MEL indicator for reach and coverage reporting to donors.']

  Note: 'Transactional record for individual capacity-building activities delivered to partner organizations including trainings, mentoring sessions, technical assistance visits, and peer learning events. Captures activity type, delivery date, facilitator, participants, topics covered, pre/post assessment scores, and completion status. Tracks progress against the capacity-building plan.'
}

Table partnership.partner_risk_register {
  partner_risk_register_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate identifier for each risk entry in the partner risk register. Primary key for this data product.']
  due_diligence_record_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to partnership.due_diligence_record. Business justification: partner_risk_register stores capacity_assessment_score and capacity_assessment_date but has no FK to due_diligence_record. Risks are identified through due diligence processes. Adding due_diligence_re']
  partner_org_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the partner organization for which this risk entry is recorded. Links to the partner master record.']
  staff_member_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the staff member record of the designated risk owner responsible for monitoring and managing this risk. Enables automated escalation workflows and accountability tracking.']
  subaward_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the specific sub-award agreement under which this risk is being assessed, if applicable. Links to the sub-award management record.']
  composite_risk_score varchar [note: 'Calculated product of likelihood_rating multiplied by impact_rating (range 1–25), yielding the overall risk severity score used to prioritise mitigation actions and sub-award oversight decisions. Stored as a business-recorded value from the risk assessment process, not a real-time derived metric.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this risk register entry was first created in the system. Provides the audit trail creation marker required for data governance and compliance reporting.']
  donor_notification_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the risk event or materialisation requires formal notification to the donor per grant agreement terms (True). Relevant for USAID, DFID/FCDO, CERF, and other institutional donors with mandatory incident reporting clauses.']
  donor_notified_date date [note: 'Date on which the donor was formally notified of this risk or incident. Null if notification has not yet occurred or is not required. Used for compliance tracking against donor agreement notification timelines.']
  due_diligence_level varchar [note: 'Level of due diligence applied to this partner in relation to this risk: standard (routine checks), enhanced (additional scrutiny for high-risk partners), simplified (low-risk, minimal checks). Aligns with donor-mandated partner vetting requirements.']
  end_date date
  escalated_to varchar [note: 'Name or role of the individual, committee, or external body to whom this risk was escalated (e.g., \'Country Director\', \'Board Risk Committee\', \'USAID Agreement Officer\'). Supports accountability and audit trail requirements.']
  escalation_date date [note: 'Date on which this risk was formally escalated to senior management, the board, or the donor. Null if escalation has not occurred. Used for audit trail and compliance reporting.']
  escalation_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this risk has been flagged for escalation to senior management, the board, or the donor (True). Set automatically when risk_level is \'critical\' or when safeguarding_risk_flag is True.']
  fiduciary_risk_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this risk entry has been classified as a fiduciary risk (True) involving financial management, fund accountability, or procurement integrity concerns. Triggers enhanced financial monitoring protocols.']
  financial_exposure_usd decimal(18,2) [note: 'Estimated maximum financial exposure in US Dollars associated with this risk, representing the value of funds at risk if the risk materialises (e.g., sub-award value at risk of misappropriation). Used in fiduciary risk prioritisation and BvA oversight.']
  impact_rating varchar [note: 'Numeric score (1–5) representing the severity of consequences if the risk materialises: 1=Negligible, 2=Minor, 3=Moderate, 4=Major, 5=Catastrophic. Assessed across financial, programmatic, reputational, and safeguarding dimensions.']
  inherent_impact_rating varchar [note: 'Impact rating (1–5) assessed BEFORE any mitigation controls are applied. Together with inherent_likelihood_rating, establishes the gross risk score prior to control application.']
  inherent_likelihood_rating varchar [note: 'Likelihood rating (1–5) assessed BEFORE any mitigation controls are applied. Captures the gross/inherent risk level to benchmark the effectiveness of mitigation measures.']
  last_review_date date [note: 'The date on which this risk entry was most recently reviewed and updated by the risk owner or oversight team. Used to flag stale entries requiring re-assessment.']
  likelihood_rating varchar [note: 'Numeric score (1–5) representing the probability that the risk will materialise: 1=Rare, 2=Unlikely, 3=Possible, 4=Likely, 5=Almost Certain. Used in composite risk scoring per standard NGO risk matrices.']
  mitigation_measures varchar [note: 'Narrative description of the specific controls, actions, and safeguards implemented or planned to reduce the likelihood or impact of the risk. May include capacity-building, enhanced financial monitoring, spot-checks, or escalation protocols.']
  mitigation_status varchar [note: 'Current implementation status of the mitigation measures: planned (not yet started), in_progress (underway), completed (fully implemented), overdue (past target date without completion).']
  modified_timestamp timestamp
  monitoring_frequency varchar [note: 'Frequency at which this risk entry is actively monitored and reviewed: weekly, monthly, quarterly, semi_annual, annual, or ad_hoc. Drives scheduling of oversight activities and MEL review cycles.']
  next_review_date date [note: 'Scheduled date for the next formal review of this risk entry. Drives automated reminders and compliance with periodic risk review obligations under donor agreements.']
  notes varchar [note: 'Free-text field for additional context, observations, or supplementary information related to this risk entry that does not fit into structured fields. May include references to related incident reports, audit findings, or SitRep entries.']
  oversight_mechanism varchar [note: 'Description of the specific oversight mechanism applied to manage this risk (e.g., \'Monthly financial spot-checks\', \'Quarterly field monitoring visits\', \'Third-party audit\', \'PDM surveys\'). Documents the control environment for donor compliance.']
  partner_risk_register_code varchar
  partner_risk_register_description varchar
  partner_risk_register_name varchar
  partner_risk_register_status varchar
  risk_appetite_alignment varchar [note: 'Assessment of whether this risk falls within the organisation\'s defined risk appetite: within_appetite (acceptable), at_tolerance (borderline, requires monitoring), exceeds_appetite (unacceptable, requires immediate action or sub-award suspension).']
  risk_category varchar [note: 'High-level classification of the risk type: fiduciary (financial mismanagement, fraud), programmatic (delivery failure, quality gaps), reputational (media, political exposure), safeguarding (protection of beneficiaries and staff), or compliance (regulatory, donor-condition breaches).']
  risk_closure_date date [note: 'The date on which this risk was formally closed, either because it was fully mitigated, the sub-award ended, or the risk was deemed no longer applicable. Null if the risk remains open.']
  risk_description varchar [note: 'Detailed narrative describing the nature of the risk, its potential causes, and the context in which it may materialise. Supports due diligence documentation and donor compliance reporting.']
  risk_identification_date date [note: 'The date on which this risk was first formally identified and entered into the risk register. Marks the start of the risk lifecycle and is used for ageing analysis.']
  risk_level varchar [note: 'Qualitative risk band derived from the composite risk score: low (1–4), medium (5–9), high (10–16), critical (17–25). Used for traffic-light reporting in MEL dashboards, donor SitReps, and sub-award oversight decisions.']
  risk_materialisation_date date [note: 'Date on which the risk was confirmed to have materialised into an actual incident or adverse event. Null if the risk has not materialised. Used for incident timeline analysis and donor reporting.']
  risk_materialised boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the identified risk has actually materialised into an incident or adverse event (True). When True, triggers incident management workflows and may require sub-award suspension or termination review.']
  risk_owner varchar [note: 'Name or role title of the individual within the NGO responsible for monitoring and managing this risk entry. Typically a Program Manager, Grants Manager, or Country Director.']
  risk_register_code varchar [note: 'Externally-known unique alphanumeric code assigned to this risk entry for cross-system reference and reporting (e.g., RR-FISC-2024-0012). Used in donor reports, audit trails, and compliance filings.']
  risk_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the risk entry: open (identified, not yet addressed), under_review (being assessed), mitigated (controls applied), escalated (elevated to senior management or donor), closed (resolved or no longer applicable).']
  risk_subcategory varchar [note: 'Granular classification within the risk category (e.g., \'Procurement Fraud\' under fiduciary, \'GBV Incident\' under safeguarding, \'FCPA Violation\' under compliance). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: procurement_fraud|financial_misreporting|conflict_of_interest|gbv_incident|child_protection|data_breach|political_interference|media_exposure|delivery_failure|quality_failure|regulatory_breach|donor_condition_breach — promote to reference product]']
  risk_title varchar [note: 'Short, human-readable title summarising the risk (e.g., \'Inadequate financial controls at field office level\'). Used as the primary label in risk dashboards and SitRep summaries.']
  safeguarding_risk_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this risk entry involves safeguarding concerns (True), including GBV, child protection, or protection of beneficiaries and staff from exploitation and abuse. Triggers mandatory escalation per CHS safeguarding protocols.']
  start_date date
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this risk register entry was most recently modified. Used for change tracking, audit trail, and data lineage in the Databricks Silver Layer.']

  Note: 'Master record maintaining the risk register for each partner organization covering fiduciary risk, programmatic risk, reputational risk, safeguarding risk, and compliance risk. Captures risk category, risk description, likelihood rating, impact rating, composite risk score, mitigation measures, risk owner, and review date. Feeds into sub-award management and oversight decisions.'
}

Existence Justification: In nonprofit operations, partner organizations are subject to multiple compliance obligations (IRS filings, donor reporting, audit requirements, registration renewals), and each compliance obligation applies to multiple partner organizations. The NGO actively manages partner compliance tracking as an operational process: assigning obligations to partners, monitoring due dates, tracking completion status, and escalating overdue items. This is not an analytical correlation but an operational business process where compliance officers create, update, and monitor partner-specific compliance assignments.'

  donor_reporting_frequency varchar [note: 'The frequency at which financial reports must be submitted to the donor for this budget. Drives the cadence of Budget vs. Actual (BvA) reporting and compliance monitoring.']

Table finance.nicra_rate {
  nicra_rate_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for nicra_rate']
  created_by_staff_member_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to workforce.staff_member. Business justification: Finance tracks which staff member created each NICRA rate for accountability in indirect cost rate management and compliance.']
  nicra_agreement_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to compliance.nicra_agreement. Business justification: Finance nicra_rate table operationalizes rates from compliance nicra_agreement. Finance applies rates; compliance maintains agreement terms. Link ensures rate application matches negotiated agreement ']
  administrative_rate decimal(5,2) [note: 'The administrative component of the Facilities and Administration (F&A) rate, if the NICRA separates facilities and administrative costs. This rate covers general administration, departmental administration, and sponsored projects administration.']
  agreement_number varchar [note: 'The official agreement number assigned by the cognizant federal agency to this Negotiated Indirect Cost Rate Agreement. This is the externally-known identifier used in grant reporting and compliance documentation.']
  agreement_status varchar [note: 'The current lifecycle status of the NICRA agreement. Draft indicates the agreement is being prepared; pending approval means it has been submitted to the cognizant agency; approved means the agency has accepted it; active means it is currently in effect; expired means the effective period has ended; superseded means a newer agreement has replaced it; terminated means it was cancelled before expiration. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: draft|pending_approval|approved|active|expired|superseded|terminated — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  approval_date date [note: 'The date on which the cognizant federal agency officially approved the NICRA agreement. This may differ from the negotiation date if there was a review period.']
  audit_period_end_date date [note: 'The end date of the audit period on which this NICRA rate is based. For final rates, this is the period for which actual costs were audited to establish the rate.']
  audit_period_start_date date [note: 'The start date of the audit period on which this NICRA rate is based. For final rates, this is the period for which actual costs were audited to establish the rate.']
  carryforward_adjustment_amount decimal(15,2) [note: 'The dollar amount of carryforward adjustment from prior periods that must be applied when using this rate. Carryforward adjustments occur when provisional rates differ from final rates, requiring reconciliation in subsequent periods. [framework] Recognized/measured per configurable accounting framework: IPSAS, US GAAP ASC 958, Form 990 (IPSAS for UN agencies; US GAAP ASC 958 / Form 990 for US nonprofits).']
  cognizant_agency_code varchar [note: 'The code identifying the federal agency responsible for negotiating and approving this indirect cost rate agreement. Common cognizant agencies include USAID, HHS, USDA, and DOD. The cognizant agency is typically the agency providing the most federal funding to the organization.']
  cognizant_agency_name varchar [note: 'The full name of the federal agency responsible for negotiating and approving this indirect cost rate agreement (e.g., United States Agency for International Development, Department of Health and Human Services).']
  cost_base_type varchar [note: 'The cost base to which the indirect cost rate is applied. Modified Total Direct Costs (MTDC) is the most common base and excludes capital expenditures, equipment, subawards over $25K, and other specific costs. Total Direct Costs includes all direct costs. Salaries and Wages base applies the rate only to personnel costs. [framework] Recognized/measured per configurable accounting framework: IPSAS, US GAAP ASC 958, Form 990 (IPSAS for UN agencies; US GAAP ASC 958 / Form 990 for US nonprofits).']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when this NICRA rate record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.']
  de_minimis_rate_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this record represents the use of the de minimis indirect cost rate. Organizations that have never received a negotiated rate may elect to use a de minimis rate of 10% of Modified Total Direct Costs per OMB Uniform Guidance.']
  document_reference_url varchar [note: 'URL or file path to the official NICRA agreement document. This provides direct access to the signed agreement for audit and compliance purposes.']
  effective_end_date date [note: 'The date on which this negotiated indirect cost rate expires and is no longer applicable to federal grants. This is the end of the rate period as specified in the NICRA agreement. Nullable for open-ended agreements pending renegotiation.']
  effective_start_date date [note: 'The date on which this negotiated indirect cost rate becomes effective and can be applied to federal grants. This is the beginning of the rate period as specified in the NICRA agreement.']
  facilities_rate decimal(5,2) [note: 'The facilities component of the Facilities and Administration (F&A) rate, if the NICRA separates facilities and administrative costs. This rate covers depreciation, operations and maintenance, library, and other facility-related costs.']
  fiscal_year varchar [note: 'The fiscal year to which this NICRA rate applies. Format typically YYYY or YYYY-YYYY for multi-year agreements. This helps track which rate applies to which grant period.']
  fringe_benefit_rate decimal(5,2) [note: 'The negotiated fringe benefit rate expressed as a percentage, if included in the NICRA agreement. Fringe benefits are often negotiated alongside indirect cost rates and applied to salaries and wages to calculate total personnel costs.']
  is_active boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this NICRA rate is currently active and should be used for indirect cost calculations on new grants. True means the rate is within its effective period and approved for use; False means it is expired, superseded, or not yet effective.']
  last_modified_by_user varchar [note: 'The username or identifier of the user who last modified this NICRA rate record in the system. Used for audit trail and accountability.']
  last_modified_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when this NICRA rate record was last updated in the system. Used for audit trail and change tracking.']
  negotiation_date date [note: 'The date on which the indirect cost rate was formally negotiated and agreed upon with the cognizant federal agency. This is the date the NICRA agreement was signed.']
  organizational_unit_code varchar [note: 'The code identifying the organizational unit (division, department, or legal entity) to which this NICRA rate applies. Some organizations negotiate separate rates for different divisions or subsidiaries.']
  organizational_unit_name varchar [note: 'The name of the organizational unit (division, department, or legal entity) to which this NICRA rate applies.']
  rate_category varchar [note: 'The functional category or pool to which this rate applies. Organizations may have multiple rate categories such as headquarters operations, field operations, research, or program-specific pools. This allows for different indirect cost rates for different types of activities.']
  rate_percentage decimal(5,2) [note: 'The negotiated indirect cost rate expressed as a percentage. This rate is applied to the applicable cost base to calculate allowable indirect cost recovery on federally-funded grants. For example, a rate of 15.50 means 15.50% of the base can be recovered as indirect costs.']
  rate_type varchar [note: 'The type of indirect cost rate negotiated with the federal government. Predetermined rates are negotiated in advance for a future period; fixed rates are established for a specific period and not subject to adjustment; provisional rates are temporary rates subject to adjustment; final rates are established after costs are known and audited.']
  special_remarks varchar [note: 'Free-text field capturing any special conditions, limitations, or instructions specified in the NICRA agreement. This may include restrictions on which grants the rate applies to, special calculation methods, or other agency-imposed conditions.']
  successor_agreement_number varchar [note: 'The agreement number of the subsequent NICRA that supersedes or replaces this agreement. Populated when a new rate is negotiated.']

  Note: 'Negotiated Indirect Cost Rate Agreement (NICRA) master record defining the approved indirect cost rates negotiated with the US federal government (typically USAID or HHS). Captures NICRA agreement number, rate type (predetermined, fixed, provisional, final), applicable base (modified total direct costs, total direct costs, salaries and wages), rate percentage, effective start and end dates, cognizant federal agency, agreement status, and applicable organizational unit. Used for indirect cost recovery calculations on federally-funded grants per OMB 2 CFR 200. | Accounting framework: configurable for US GAAP (ASC 958), IPSAS (UN/INGO), or IFRS as applicable. [accounting_framework] Accounting framework references (configurable): IPSAS (UN agencies); US GAAP ASC 958 (US nonprofits, currently the only reference); Form 990 (US IRS, currently referenced). IPSAS is recognized alongside US GAAP (ASC 958) and Form 990; framework applied per reporting entity. Systems-of-record: SAP CO, cognizant agency submissions. Framework: 2 CFR 200.414 (Indirect Costs) / IPSAS 18 segment allocation.'
}

  overdraft_protection_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this bank account has overdraft protection enabled. True if overdraft protection is active; false otherwise. Overdraft protection allows transactions to proceed even if the account balance is insufficient, subject to bank terms.']
  reconciliation_frequency varchar [note: 'The required frequency for reconciling this bank account against the General Ledger (GL). High-volume or high-risk accounts may require daily reconciliation; lower-activity accounts may be reconciled monthly or quarterly per internal controls policy.']
  routing_number varchar [note: 'The 9-digit routing transit number (RTN) used in the United States for domestic wire transfers, ACH transactions, and check processing. Identifies the financial institution in the US banking system.']
  signatory_requirement varchar [note: 'The number and level of authorized signatories required to approve transactions on this bank account.   signatory_threshold_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'The monetary threshold above which elevated signatory requirements apply. For example, transactions below this amount may require single signatory, while transactions above require dual or board approval. Denominated in the account currency. [framework] Recognized/measured per configurable accounting framework: IPSAS, US GAAP ASC 958, Form 990 (IPSAS for UN agencies; US GAAP ASC 958 / Form 990 for US nonprofits).']
  swift_code varchar [note: 'The Society for Worldwide Interbank Financial Telecommunication (SWIFT) code, also known as Bank Identifier Code (BIC).   updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when this bank account record was last updated in the system. Supports audit trail and change tracking.']

  Note: 'Master record for all organizational bank accounts managed by the NGO across headquarters, regional offices, and country offices. Table finance.exchange_rate {
  exchange_rate_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique identifier for the exchange rate record. Primary key for the exchange rate reference master.']
  created_by_staff_member_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to workforce.staff_member. Business justification: Finance tracks which staff member created each exchange rate for accountability in foreign exchange rate management and multi-currency operations.']
  from_exchange_rate_id varchar [note: 'Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code representing the source currency in the exchange rate pair (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). The currency being converted from.']
  primary_superseded_by_rate_exchange_rate_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the exchange rate record that replaces this rate. Nullable for current active rates. Creates a chain of rate succession for historical tracking and audit purposes.']
  to_exchange_rate_id varchar [note: 'Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code representing the target currency in the exchange rate pair (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). The currency being converted to.']
  approval_required_flag boolean [note: 'Boolean indicator specifying whether this exchange rate requires formal approval before being activated for use in financial transactions. True indicates approval workflow is required; false indicates rate can be used immediately upon publication.']
  approval_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this exchange rate was formally approved for use. Nullable for rates that do not require approval. Establishes the point at which the rate became authorized for financial transactions.']
  approved_by_user varchar [note: 'Username or identifier of the authorized user who approved this exchange rate for use in financial transactions. Nullable for rates that do not require approval. Supports audit trail and accountability.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this exchange rate record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail and data lineage tracking.']
  donor_required_rate_flag boolean [note: 'Boolean indicator specifying whether this exchange rate is mandated by a specific donor or grant agreement. True indicates the rate must be used for specific donor reporting; false indicates it is a general organizational rate. Critical for grant compliance.']
  effective_date date [note: 'The date from which this exchange rate becomes valid and should be used for currency conversions. Represents the start of the rate\'s applicability period.']
  expiration_date date [note: 'The date on which this exchange rate ceases to be valid. Nullable for rates that remain effective until superseded. Represents the end of the rate\'s applicability period.']
  fiscal_period_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to finance.fiscal_period. Business justification: Exchange rates are effective for fiscal periods and used for multi-currency financial reporting and revaluation. The existing fiscal_year (INT) and fiscal_period (STRING) columns are denormalized repr']
  inverse_rate_value decimal(18,6) [note: 'The inverse of the exchange rate value, representing how many units of the source currency equal one unit of the target currency. Calculated as 1 divided by exchange_rate_value. Facilitates bidirectional currency conversions.']
  last_modified_by_user varchar [note: 'Username or identifier of the user who most recently modified this exchange rate record. Tracks responsibility for the latest changes and supports audit trail requirements.']
  last_modified_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this exchange rate record was most recently updated. Tracks the latest change to any field in the record for audit and data quality purposes.']
  mid_market_rate_flag boolean [note: 'Boolean indicator specifying whether this rate represents the mid-market rate (the midpoint between buy and sell rates). True indicates a neutral market rate without spread markup; false indicates a rate that may include transaction costs or spreads.']
  notes varchar [note: 'Free-text field for additional context, special instructions, or explanatory remarks about this exchange rate. May include information about unusual market conditions, donor-specific requirements, or deviations from standard rate sources.']
  rate_calculation_method varchar [note: 'Description of the methodology used to calculate or derive the exchange rate. For average rates, describes the averaging period and calculation approach. For budget rates, describes the forecasting methodology. Ensures transparency in rate determination.']
  rate_publication_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The exact date and time when the exchange rate was officially published or released by the rate source. Provides precise temporal reference for rate validity and audit purposes.']
  rate_source varchar [note: 'The authoritative source or provider of the exchange rate data. Examples include central banks (Federal Reserve, European Central Bank), commercial providers (OANDA, Bloomberg, Reuters), UN Operational Rates of Exchange, or internal treasury systems. Ensures traceability and auditability of rate origins.']
  rate_source_reference varchar [note: 'External reference identifier or URL from the rate source system that can be used to verify or trace back to the original rate publication. Supports audit trail and compliance verification.']
  rate_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the exchange rate record. Active rates are currently in use, inactive rates are no longer valid, superseded rates have been replaced by newer rates, pending rates are awaiting approval, and draft rates are under preparation.']
  rate_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the exchange rate indicating its purpose and calculation method. Spot rates are real-time market rates, average rates are period averages, budget rates are planning rates, closing rates are end-of-period rates, forward rates are future-dated contracts, and historical rates are past reference rates.']
  revaluation_rate_flag boolean [note: 'Boolean indicator specifying whether this rate is designated for use in general ledger foreign currency revaluation processes. True indicates the rate should be used for balance sheet revaluation; false indicates it is for transactional purposes only.']
  spread_percentage decimal(5,4) [note: 'The percentage spread or markup applied to the base exchange rate to account for transaction costs, bank fees, or foreign exchange margins. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.0150 for 1.5%). Nullable for rates without spreads.']
  un_operational_rate_flag boolean [note: 'Boolean indicator specifying whether this rate is sourced from the United Nations Operational Rates of Exchange, commonly used by international NGOs and humanitarian organizations for standardized multi-currency reporting.']
  usage_context varchar [note: 'Description of the specific business contexts or transaction types for which this exchange rate should be used. Examples include donor reporting, budget planning, accounts payable processing, grant financial statements, or general ledger revaluation. Provides guidance for appropriate rate application.']
  value decimal(18,6) [note: 'The numeric exchange rate value representing how many units of the target currency equal one unit of the source currency. For example, if USD to EUR rate is 0.85, then 1 USD equals 0.85 EUR. Stored with six decimal places for precision.']
  variance_from_prior_rate decimal(18,6) [note: 'The absolute difference between this exchange rate value and the immediately preceding rate for the same currency pair and rate type. Facilitates trend analysis and identification of significant rate movements.']
  variance_percentage decimal(7,4) [note: 'The percentage change between this exchange rate and the immediately preceding rate for the same currency pair and rate type. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.0250 for 2.5% increase). Supports volatility monitoring and financial risk assessment.']

  Note: 'Reference master for currency exchange rates used across all multi-currency financial transactions, grant reporting, and donor financial statements. Captures currency pair (from/to currency), rate type (spot, average, budget, closing), exchange rate value, effective date, rate source (central bank, OANDA, UN operational rate), and rate status. Supports multi-currency fund accounting, grant financial reporting in donor currencies, and FASB ASC 958 foreign currency translation. | Accounting framework: configurable for US GAAP (ASC 958), IPSAS (UN/INGO), or IFRS as applicable. [accounting_framework] Accounting framework references (configurable): IPSAS (UN agencies); US GAAP ASC 958 (US nonprofits, currently the only reference); Form 990 (US IRS, currently referenced). IPSAS is recognized alongside US GAAP (ASC 958) and Form 990; framework applied per reporting entity. Systems-of-record: UN Treasury (UNORE rates), SAP FI currency tables. Framework: IPSAS 4 (Effects of Changes in Foreign Exchange Rates) / US GAAP ASC 830.'
}

  resolution_date date [note: 'Date when all corrective actions were completed and the incident was formally closed.']

  Note: 'SSOT for regulatory and policy compliance incidents (fraud, misuse of funds, regulatory breaches, audit findings). Distinct from safeguarding.safeguarding_incident which covers PSEA, sexual exploitation, abuse, and harassment incidents.'
